question.prompt: \(f(x)=x^2\) and \(y=f(2x)\). What is the derivative of \(y\) at \(x=1\)?

solutions.explanation: \((x^2)'\) evaluated at \(2x\) is \(2\times(2x)\), then multiply by \(2\). At \(x=1\), the result is \(8\).
solutions.title: Chain rule

solutions.explanation: Substitute \(2x\) into the given formula for \(f\) before differentiating. Then \(y=f(2x)=(2x)^2=4x^2\), so the power and constant-multiple rules give \(y'=8x\). Hence \(y'(1)=8\).
solutions.title: Simplify the composition first
